changes: Registration can require a verified email: [nickserv] require_email = true (off by default, needs email_command) makes REGISTER ask for an email, and the new account does nothing (no IDENTIFY, no SASL, no nick protection) until the mailed code comes back with /msg NickServ VERIFY <code>, which also logs the user in. Clients using IRCv3 draft/account-registration get REGISTER VERIFICATION_REQUIRED and finish with the new VERIFY <account> <code> command (VERIFY SUCCESS). A registration never verified within verify_window_hours (default 24) is dropped so the name is free again; existing accounts are untouched; services admins can ACTIVATE <account> by hand. Wrong VERIFY codes now count against the per-IP limit like wrong passwords

NickServ account expiry: [nickserv] expire_days (0 = never, the default) drops an account nobody has logged in to for that long, with its grouped nicks; an account logged in right now counts as used, and services admins, [[opers]] accounts, suspended accounts and any an admin marks with NOEXPIRE <account> ON never expire. INFO shows when an account expires. expire_warn_days mails the verified address first (email_command gets purpose "expire" and the days left). Accounts with no login on record start their clock at the first check, so upgrading expires nothing at once. Dropping an account (DROP, FDROP, expiry) now also removes it from ChanServ as a channel's founder, =account access entry and successor: before, whoever registered the same name later inherited those channels. The config wizard and tools/makeconf.py ask for both NickServ and ChanServ expiry

Planned maintenance can be announced on IRC: a "tell users on IRC" box on each window sends every connected user a server notice when it is planned, reminders before it starts ([announce] reminders in stats.toml, 24h and 1h by default) and a cancellation if the window is removed. The panel queues them in stats/announce.queue, services sends them to the hub (SVCGLOBAL, needs the collector on), and the hub passes them to every server (GNOTICE; older servers ignore it). Off unless ticked

Stats panel: the public page (public = true, and [export] public_html) no longer shows software versions, CPU or memory, and says only what kind of outage a split was (Ping timeout, Closed by an operator, Connection lost) instead of SQUIT reasons with oper nicks; viewer logins see what they did before. New for admins on the Maintenance section: planned maintenance windows (splits in them don't count against uptime, alerts stay quiet, the next 7 days' windows are announced on every page), per-server map position, location label and hiding (over stats.toml [[servers]]), merging a renamed server's history into its new name (also netstats.py admin merge OLD NEW), and an activity log of logins, failed logins and admin actions. Alerts: [alerts] webhook posts when a link is down for down_minutes, services stop reporting, a probed port stops answering, or a TLS certificate is about to expire; once when it starts, once when it's fixed, with a test button

Stats panel hardening: a 30 s request timeout against clients that stall, a negative Content-Length refused, a login with an unknown name costs the same scrypt as a known one (the time no longer tells which names exist), the failed-login table is pruned, and every POST must come from the panel's own pages (an Origin check on top of the SameSite cookie; the referrer policy is now same-origin, so a browser sends that Origin)

Stats panel: a Maintenance section for admins. Forget a server that was retired (its history, outages, health checks and location go, and it leaves the map and the tables; it comes back on its own if it ever links again), or every server not linked at once; clear past incidents or the ban history; run the health checks or the location lookup now; compact the database. Each action needs the admin's login session and its page's form token, asks before deleting, and is logged with the login's name. The same actions run from a shell: netstats.py admin forget NAME, forget-gone, clear-incidents, clear-bans, reprobe, relocate, vacuum

Server links: a KILL or UNGLINE from a source the link can't speak for (a made-up UID or SID, or one on another branch of the network) was obeyed, which also slipped past the hub's oper_scope = local check for a leaf; it is now dropped. An SJOIN only brings users from the sender's side, and a SERVER line (or the dialed hub's reply) with a malformed SID or server name closes the link, as the accepting side already did. tests/itest/test_star.py runs a hub with two leaves (one limited): leaf-to-leaf traffic, a split and relink of one leaf, oper reach, G-lines and a remote SQUIT

tools/upgrade.py on an install that is not a git checkout (a source tarball, or a copy unpacked inside some other git repository, where git answered for the wrong repository and an upgrade would have checked out and reset it): --check crashed with a traceback and an upgrade stopped with "needs a git clone" and no way forward. It now says what is missing (no .git, no commits, no origin; --check and --rollback exit 11) and the interactive run offers to turn the install into a checkout: only a .git folder is written, no file of yours is touched (undo with rm -rf .git). It picks the commit your files match best (the release version.h names, or main, since a tarball of main still names the last release), shows the files that differ, and keeps them through the upgrade. --yes alone never converts; --convert does, and --origin points it at a mirror or fork. tests/itest/test_upgrade_clone.py covers it

tools/upgrade.py checks linger when the systemd user units are enabled, and turns it on when it may (otherwise it says so, with the command): without it the ircd and services stop 10 seconds after your last SSH session closes, so every user is disconnected, and an SSH client that reconnects does it again each time. The install docs now say to enable it right after enabling the units. It surfaced on a hub where the daemons restarted every ten minutes, each time an SSH session dropped and came back

--daemon now returns only once the daemon is ready (its pidfile written, its listeners open, its signal handlers installed). A Type=forking systemd unit used to log "Can't open PID file (yet?)" and "Supervising process which is not our child", so it could not tell when the ircd or services died and Restart=on-failure did nothing; and a daemon that died while starting, such as services with a corrupt accounts file, made the command report success. It now exits non-zero in that case, for the ircd and for services. tests/itest/test_daemon.py covers it

/REHASH now closes the links that its config no longer allows. Remove a [[links.peers]] entry and rehash: that peer is disconnected at once (opers see "Link with ... closed: its [[links.peers]] entry was removed", the peer is told why) and refused from then on, where before the open link stayed up until it dropped by itself and only the next connection was refused. The same happens to a link whose address an edited allowed_ips no longer lists, and to the services link when its entry is removed. A changed password or fingerprint does not close an open link (use /SQUIT), and a hub must still keep at least one entry that accepts a leaf. A refused handshake now says whether no entry has that name or the entry did not match. tests/itest/test_link_rehash.py covers it

Network operators from services: an [[opers]] entry in services.toml (account, certfp, privileges, password_only) makes an account an IRC operator on whichever server it logs in to, with no [[operators]] block on that server. When the account IDENTIFYs or logs in with SASL, services sends the user's server a new SVSOPER (older servers ignore it); every other server already trusts an oper from another server, so they reach the whole network. It needs the account's TLS client certificate to match certfp unless password_only = true, so a stolen password alone is not enough. It ends when they log out, change account or disconnect, and when the entry is removed. Edit services.toml and /REHASH the hub (it now tells services to reload with a new SVCREHASH line; `services --rehash` still works): new entries apply to users already logged in, removed ones lose oper status at once, and a file with a mistake is refused and the old list stays. [security] accept_services_opers = false makes a server ignore these grants and take back the ones it gave on /REHASH; a hub's oper_scope and oper_deny for a leaf still limit them. tests/itest/test_svc_opers.py covers it

Spam filters can be network-wide: a rule that starts with "global" in spamfilters.conf, or is added with /SPAMFILTER ADD GLOBAL <targets> <action> <duration|-> <reason> <regex>, is sent to every linked server, which enforces it as if it were its own. Put them on the hub and every leaf has them, so a spammer on a leaf that never had the rule is stopped there. A server sends its whole set whenever it changes and at every link-up (a new SPAMFILTER link message, which older servers ignore), so deleting a rule on the hub removes it everywhere and a leaf that was down catches up by itself; Any hub or leaf can add them and every server gets them (hubs pass them to their own leaves); SPAMFILTER LIST on another server shows a rule as [global from hub...], and SPAMFILTER DEL there removes it on that server at once and asks the owner, which drops it from its list and file and sends its set again. The global rules bind a server whose own [spam] is off (the module's own rules, new-connection restriction and limits stay off there), and a server checks the global rules before its own, so a leaf can't undo the hub's rule (its own rules add to them): the new action `allow` lets the text through and skips the rules below it, so an exception to a global rule is a global allow above it on the hub. A leaf the hub limits with oper_scope = "local" can't publish them. The global rules from other servers live in memory and come back with the link. tests/itest/test_spam_global.py and tests/unit.c cover it

Containers: the container/ directory has a Containerfile, an entrypoint, container/setup.sh (a guided podman install: it pulls the image, runs the config wizard in it, installs systemd user units, turns on linger, and has status, logs, rehash, upgrade, backup and uninstall), a compose.yaml for Docker, and container/README.md, a step-by-step guide to the config, logs and data directory. The image holds the ircd, services, the stats panel and the config tools for x86-64 and arm64 (a 64-bit Raspberry Pi pulls it instead of compiling). CI builds it on both architectures, runs container/smoke.sh in it (wizard, ircd + services + panel, restart, rehash, graceful stop) and publishes it to ghcr.io only after every platform is green. The stats panel now stops on SIGTERM when it runs in the foreground, as a container's PID 1 needs

[[classes]] hosts (and the other IP lists): an IPv6 glob written with zero-padded groups, such as "2602:f992:00c8:b79*", never matched, because the server spells client addresses without leading zeros ("2602:f992:c8:b793::1"); the client then fell back to the global per-IP limit and got "Too many connections from your host" although its class allowed more. The config now reads the group as "c8" when it loads and says so in the log, and tools/confcheck.py (and sekurircd --check) shows that warning. The template and docs explain how IPv6 globs are matched and recommend CIDR ranges. tests/unit.c and tests/itest/test_ipv6.py cover it

A plain IPv6 address in the config's IP lists now matches: "::1" never did, because the server spells client addresses "0::1" and these lists are compared as text. It is rewritten when the config loads (and a glob starting with "::" gets the same leading 0) in webirc hosts, [server] proxy_protocol_hosts, [websocket] trusted_proxies, link allowed_ips, the protection bundle's exempt ips and [[classes]] hosts. CIDR ranges were never affected

[[classes]] hosts: a plain IPv6 address such as "::1" (or a glob starting with "::") never matched a client, because the server spells client addresses "0::1"; it is now rewritten when the config loads. IPv4 and IPv6 (globs and CIDR ranges such as "10.0.0.0/8", "2001:db8::/32") can be mixed in one hosts list, and the template and docs now say so

Limit what a leaf's opers can do to the rest of the network, set on the hub per leaf: [[links.peers]] oper_scope = "local" keeps that leaf's opers to their own server (no KILL, SAJOIN/SAPART/SANICK/CHGHOST/CHGIDENT, GLINE/SHUN, SQUIT, REHASH or STATS aimed at another server) and oper_deny = ["override", "auspex"] takes privileges off them (any of kill, kline, sa, host, wallops, rehash, die, link, override, auspex, immune, all). The leaf needs no setting: the hub tells it when it links and on every /REHASH, the leaf refuses with a clear message, and the hub drops it anyway if an older leaf sends it. Hub opers are never limited. Without the keys nothing changes. tests/itest/test_oper_scope.py covers it

The stats panel has a real login form and a Log out button. It used to ask for the password with the browser's own Basic-auth box, which has no way to log out. /login is now a form (name + password) and a successful login gives the browser a session cookie (HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict, Secure on HTTPS, 12 hours) that Log out ends at once; the old cookie stops working, and removing a login with netstats.py --user --del (or changing its password) ends its sessions too. A logged-in browser always lives at /admin/. The Log in / Log out button and the Admin/Viewer badge moved to the right of the section bar, under the Light/Dark toggle. curl -u and other scripts that send HTTP Basic credentials keep working, and a failed login still counts toward the 10-in-10-minutes lockout. A panel started before this needs ./sekurircd restart-stats. netstats.py selftest covers the login, session and logout flow

The stats line in the debug channel no longer says "services: not running (stale pidfile ...)" for a server that is not supposed to run services. A leaf (links mode "leaf") skips the services check altogether, since only the hub runs services, and a config that still names the old services/chanserv.pid now looks at the live services.pid first, so a leftover chanserv.pid cannot hide it. ./sekurircd also deletes a dead old chanserv.pid when it starts

Short MOTD: put an ircd.smotd next to ircd.motd (same name, .smotd) and it is shown on connect, while /MOTD shows the full ircd.motd. If only one of the two exists, it is used for both. REHASH reloads it. config/ircd.template.smotd is a colored one to start from (cp it to ircd.smotd): the banner, TLS port, lobby, NickServ/ChanServ HELP, the rules in one line and a pointer to /MOTD for the complete one
Bot MOTD: an optional bot.motd next to the config file is shown to a user when they set user mode +B (bot)

WHOIS "seconds idle" only resets when the user sends a PRIVMSG, as on other ircds. It used to reset on every byte the server read from them, so a client's automatic PING/PONG keepalives, a CTCP reply (a NOTICE) or typing/reaction TAGMSGs kept the idle counter at zero or made it jump back to a few seconds. The ping-timeout clock is separate and unchanged. A PRIVMSG that fails (no such nick, blocked, flood-dropped) no longer counts, always-on users keep their idle time when they reattach, STATS o shows the same idle, and WHOX %l (idle) now follows +I (hide idle) and is 0 for users on other servers instead of a made-up number

More client ports: [server] extra_ports = [6668, 6669] adds plaintext listeners next to port, and [tls] extra_ports = [7000, 9999] adds TLS ones (same certificate; up to 16 of each, IPv6 twins when ipv6 is on). REHASH opens the new ones and closes the removed ones without dropping anyone; a port that is already taken is logged and skipped, and one that clashes with another listener's port is refused when the config is checked. STATS P lists them, the IRCv3 STS policy still names tls.port

makeconf's own check no longer refuses a leaf's config: a missing services/services.toml is optional in tools/confcheck.py (a leaf uses its hub's NickServ/ChanServ, so the wizard used to stop with 'did not accept the generated config')

A restarted leaf now tells its hub about its always-on users. It dialed the hub before restoring the sessions saved in alwayson.json, so its burst left them out: the hub answered "No such nick" for them and a SASL login on the hub started a fresh session instead of resuming, until the next relink. The hub itself was never affected. If a leaf was restarted on an older version, /SQUIT it from the hub once and it relinks with them

Network stats panel (stats/netstats.py, opt-in): an HTML dashboard with a world map of the servers and their links, users over time, every split with its real reason, link and services uptime, per-server version, CPU and memory, the connections-per-hour heatmap, account growth, protection (DNSBL hits, proxies found, spam filter actions and rules), bans and outside health checks (ports, TLS certificate days left). Turn it on with ./sekurircd enable-stats (off again: disable-stats), or answer yes in tools/makeconf.py, which also writes the admin login and sets [debug_channel] stats_interval = 300 so every server reports its numbers (a leaf is asked too). bin/services then asks the hub for a snapshot every minute plus link, split, ban and stats-line events (a new SVCSTATS service-link request, which older hubs ignore) and logs them to stats/events.log. netstats.py loads that into SQLite (per-minute data for 7 days, hourly for 90, daily for retention_days) and either serves it (./sekurircd start-stats, admin and viewer logins, optional public viewer page, optional TLS) or writes static files for a website from cron (netstats.py render). Logins: netstats.py --user --admin|--viewer --add|--del NAME, --user --status, --mkpasswd. Python 3.11+, standard library only; map positions come from the free offline DB-IP Lite database (netstats.py geoip-update) or lat/lon in stats.toml. Nothing is collected or started without stats/stats.toml. For HTTPS, set [http] hostname: netstats.py check, makeconf and the web wizard print the Caddyfile block for it (Caddy fetches the certificate), and failed logins behind a proxy count per visitor (trusted_proxies). Bound to a public address, they print the ufw/firewalld/iptables/pf commands for the port and warn when logins would travel without TLS

Netsplits now carry the real reason instead of "Link closed": "Ping timeout: 180 seconds", "Connection closed by peer", "Read error: ...", "Write error: ...", "SendQ exceeded" or "SQUIT by <oper>: <reason>", in the SQUIT every server shows its opers. The stats line also ends with the server's version and shows the spam filter ("spam filter 4 actions, 12 rules")

Rehash, network-wide like UnrealIRCd and InspIRCd: every rehash is announced to opers on every server in two lines, who did it and then what changed (or why it failed and that the old config stays). That includes a SIGHUP, such as acme.sh's reload after a certificate renewal, which used to tell no oper at all. REHASH <server> rehashes another server, which answers over the link with the usual 382 and per-line report; REHASH * rehashes them all. It needs the rehash privilege on your own server. Servers send these as a new SNOTE link message, which older servers ignore

The periodic stats line ([debug_channel] stats_interval) now reaches every server's debug channel, shown as [server] users ..., so opers see all servers from wherever they are. It now separates local and network users ("users 9 local, 17 network (peak 21)"); the rest of the line (connections, bans, DNSBL, scanner, CPU and memory) was always that server's own

tools/upgrade.py: choosing the latest release or a specific tag/commit crashed at "Updating source" with KeyError: 'branch' (only the main-branch choice worked). Nothing was changed when it crashed (backups were already made). Every choice works again

One services daemon per network, enforced: a second services daemon that links anywhere is now refused ("Services already running on <server>"), and opers are told. When two halves that each run their own link up, CAPAB now says where each side's services run, opers get an ERROR before the burst, and the older daemon is kept; the other one's link is closed. Before, nothing was detected: the second daemon sat linked doing nothing, or, on a link-up, its NickServ/ChanServ lost the nick collision but were never removed (a socketless bot marked quitting is never torn down), so it kept acting through a ghost bot the rest of the network no longer knew, with two account databases. A service also always wins a nick collision against an ordinary user now. A refused services daemon logs why and retries every 60 seconds instead of every 2, and now reads the ircd's parting ERROR (it used to give up on a hangup first). The ircd drains a closing link before closing it, so the ERROR is not lost to a TCP reset

Leaf servers made easy: tools/makeconf.py asks whether the server is a leaf; a leaf skips every services question, writes no services.toml and takes the hub's host_masking_secret so cloaks match. ./sekurircd disable-services stops this server's services and renames services/services.toml to services.toml.disabled (enable-services undoes it); start, restart and status say why services don't run (disabled, or a leaf using the hub's), and start warns when a leaf still has a services.toml. The docs have a step-by-step "adding a leaf server" (docs/configuration.html#leaf)

Oper privileges: three new [[operators]] privileges cover the oper powers that every oper used to have, whatever their privileges list said. override: join through +i/+k/+l/bans and past restrict_creation and the channel limit, talk through +m/+n/bans, kick anyone (also on +Q channels, +q users and higher ranks), MODE, TOPIC, RENAME and REDACT without ops, set +P, and message users past +D/+R/+g/+Z. auspex: see real hosts and IPs (WHOIS 378, WHO %i, WHO by real host), +i users, +p channels and idle times in WHOIS, +H opers, channel keys, CHATHISTORY of channels you're not in, and TRACE. immune: exempt from SHUN, spam filters and +f/+j. A login without privileges still gets everything; a login with a list now needs to add these to keep them, so review limited logins before upgrading. Joining a +O channel still only needs +o. SAMODE (sa) still acts as override for its own change. The old "accounts" privilege never did anything (NickServ admin commands are for [nickserv] admins in services.toml): it is still accepted, with a warning, and no longer shown in STATS O

Far connects: the new oper-only user mode +F shows "Client connecting at <server>" and "Client exiting at <server>" for users on other servers of the network, like UnrealIRCd's +F snomask. It can go in oper_modes (e.g. "+oswF"). Users arriving in a link burst or leaving in a netsplit are not announced one by one: servers now pass each other's EOB along, so every server knows when a burst ends. Before, opers saw remote users leave as a local "Client exiting" notice (one per user on a netsplit) but never saw them arrive. A server splitting off somewhere else in the network is now announced to opers on every server ("Netsplit: <uplink> <server> (reason)"), not only on the one that dropped the link
[security] default_user_modes now accepts p, I, R and D, which users could already set themselves with MODE but the config refused

STATS: much more complete. Everyone can use m (now with byte and remote counts), u (now with the 250 peak line), p (opers online), v (servers on the network) and "l <own nick>". Opers also get s (SHUNs), e (ELINEs), d (= z), b (DNSBL zones and the proxy scanner), c (connect blocks), h (hub/leaf), i (auth blocks and WEBIRC gateways), y (connection classes), P (listening ports), q (reserved nicks), t (connection and traffic totals), f (spam filters), Z (memory use) and ? (traffic per link). STATS l now has the RFC's 7 fields (sendq, messages and KB each way, time open), shows IPs while L hides them, and takes a nick for one client. K/G/Z lines now show who set them and when they expire. "STATS <letter> <server>" (or a nick on another server) is answered by that server, STATS with no or an unknown letter lists the letters you may use, and every request is shown to the opers of the server that answers it

One services daemon per network: tools/makeconf.py and the web wizard now say to answer no to running services on a leaf whose hub already runs them. tools/linkmgmt.py warns when a server with its own services dials out to another server (and says how to stop them), and when accepting a link it tells you the new server must not run its own

Links: linked servers now compare their [security] host_masking_secret when they link, through a keyed hash in CAPAB (never the secret itself). If the secrets differ, or one server has none, both servers log a warning and tell opers, because the same user would get a different cloak on each server and could dodge a cloak ban by switching. The link still comes up. tools/linkmgmt.py now prints the secret for the other server, and generates one when this server has none

TOPIC: anyone can now read the topic of a public channel without joining it, as LIST already shows it and as most ircds allow. +s and +p channels still answer "You're not on that channel", and changing a topic still needs membership

tools/linkmgmt.py: a TLS link on a server whose [tls] was off used to be written and then refused by the ircd. When the certificate files exist it now turns [tls] on in the same diff; when they don't, it shows how to get one and writes nothing. A new `certs` command (and menu item) explains self-signed versus Let's Encrypt certificates for links. The pinning note now warns that every renewal changes the fingerprint, an empty cert_file no longer shows an "Is a directory" error, and the restart hint names the -c config it was run on

Tests: a real hub + leaf pair (mode "hub" / "leaf") checks that both servers report identical channels, modes, topics, ban lists and users after each step, including a burst of random actions and a netsplit with changes on both sides

Always-on across servers: logging in with SASL on any server of the network now resumes a session detached on another one. That server drops the kept session (its channels see a QUIT "Session resumed on <server>"), and the new connection takes its nick, rejoins its channels and gets its ranks back. Servers tell each other which users are detached with a new DETACH link message; older servers ignore it

Restarts keep channel state too: alwayson.json now also saves the modes, key, limit, topic and ban/exception/invite lists of every channel an always-on user is in, and of every +P channel (which used to come back empty, or not at all). A file from the previous version still loads

WebSocket: when a client sent more frames at once than fit in one 4 KB read (a long multiline paste from a web client, say), the frame left over for the next read came out garbled: it had already been unmasked in place and was unmasked a second time. It now arrives intact

ChanServ: someone already on a channel's access list could guess its founder password as fast as they could send commands, because the last word of each command is tried as the password and a miss was never counted. A miss now starts a 3-second cooldown of its own (it doesn't trip the "too many failed attempts" of a real password)
The 005 (RPL_ISUPPORT) tokens are now sent in alphabetical order, which makes them easier to scan. Clients find tokens by name, so nothing else changes
CAP LS and CAP LIST now list the capabilities in alphabetical order too (a draft/ prefix is ignored when sorting)
A detached always-on session no longer holds on to the send and receive buffers from its last moments online
Removed code nothing called: the account-replication hooks in the account store, a few unused helpers, and the ircd no longer links the account store or SCRAM code, which only services use

Always-on sessions survive an ircd restart: every always-on user (detached, or still connected when the server stops) is saved to alwayson.json next to the config (on shutdown and every minute, so a crash loses at most a minute) and comes back detached, in the same channels with the same status, ready to resume with SASL. The expiry counts from when the user actually disconnected, through restarts and downtime, so someone who never comes back still expires after always_on_expire_days. always_on_expire_days = 0 now means never instead of until the next restart

The TOML parser is now tomlc17 (R261109), which replaces the obsolete tomlc99 for sekurircd.toml, protection.toml and services.toml. It follows TOML 1.1, so inline tables can span lines and take a trailing comma, and it is stricter about invalid dates, numbers and control characters. Existing configs parse to the same settings; parse errors now read like "(line 3) duplicate key"

NickServ HELP is now a full command reference like ChanServ's: every command with its syntax and what it does, grouped into Account, Settings, Nicks and Lookups, with commands that need a login marked *. Services admins also see the admin commands

Always-on, like Ergo's: /msg NickServ SET ALWAYS-ON ON keeps your nick online after your connection drops (or you /QUIT): it stays in its channels with its modes, marked away "Detached (always-on)", and nobody sees a QUIT. Reconnecting to the same server with SASL resumes it: you get the nick back with your channels replayed (JOIN, topic, NAMES), and others see no QUIT or JOIN, only the away status clearing. A second SASL login while you are connected takes the session over and closes the old connection (one connection at a time). Your visible user@host stays the same, so no CHGHOST. Use CHATHISTORY for what you missed. A detached session ends when an oper KILLs it, you log out, SET ALWAYS-ON OFF, or after [nickserv] always_on_expire_days (default 30, 0 = never). Operator status is not kept. Admins can turn it off with [nickserv] always_on = false in services.toml. Needs the matching ircd (SVSLOGIN gets an optional 4th parameter)

ChanServ no longer needs the channel password when you are logged in to NickServ or SASL (services 1.5.0). The founder account can run every command; an =account ACCESS entry can run what its level allows: v voices/invites/unbans itself; h adds KICK, TOPIC and the TOPIC* commands, and voice/invite/unban for others; o adds OP/DEOP and AKICK; a adds TOPICLOCK and ACCESS ADD/DEL below its own level; q adds SET and JOIN/PART; DROP, SETPASS, SET FOUNDER and SUCCESSOR stay with the founder. The password still works for everything, and a password typed out of habit is removed, so it never shows up in a topic or kick reason. Protection, as in Anope: KICK and the DE* commands refuse a target whose access is at or above yours (the founder can act on anyone). Hostmask ACCESS entries still only give modes on join

NickServ LISTLOGINS lists every connection logged in to your account (nick, user@host, server). LISTCHANS lists the registered channels you are founder of or have an =account ACCESS entry in. STATUS <nick> (Anope reply) and ACC <nick> (Atheme reply) tell bots whether a nick is logged in to the account that owns it: 3 yes, 1 online but not, 0 offline or unregistered

ChanServ TOPICAPPEND, TOPICPREPEND and TOPICSWAP #chan ... <password>: add text after or before the current topic (joined with " | "), or replace the first <search> with <replace> (TOPICSWAP #chan old:new). A result over TOPICLEN (307) is refused rather than cut. Under TOPICLOCK the new topic becomes the locked one, as with TOPIC. Needs the matching ircd (new SVCTOPIC <chan> link request)

NickServ SET AJOIN <#chan,...>|OFF: an account can list up to 10 channels it joins at every login (IDENTIFY, REGISTER, SASL). The hub joins through the normal JOIN checks, so bans, +i, +k, +l, +R and +z still apply and a refusal is announced as usual; channels already joined are skipped quietly. INFO shows the list to the owner and services admins

ISUPPORT now tells the truth about three limits: TARGMAX lists JOIN, PART and WHOIS with no limit (they take comma lists, as before), AWAYLEN=399 matches what is stored, and KICK reasons are cut to KICKLEN=300 bytes (on a character boundary) before they are sent to the channel

NickServ: after IDENTIFY or a SASL login it now tells you where and when the account last logged in ("Last login from: ~user@host on Nov 06 02:17:10 2026 +0000."), so a login you did not make stands out. INFO shows it too, to the account owner and services admins. The first login after upgrading only records it

tools/backup-config.sh --restore [ARCHIVE|DIR] restores a config backup: it lists the backups to pick from, shows which files are new or changed, backs up the current files first, then runs confcheck (and the daemons' --check) on the result and rolls back if it fails. Archives with paths outside config/ and services/ are refused

confcheck --fix --write now also fixes the file permissions it warns about (chmod 600 on config files, backups and the TLS key, go-w on config directories), for files you own; ones needing sudo or a chown are still left to you. --fix alone previews them

Config wizard: tools/makeconf.py (also sekurircd --makeconf) asks a few questions and writes a complete sekurircd.toml and, for NickServ + ChanServ, a matching services.toml. Passwords are hashed with scrypt, files are written 0600, existing ones are backed up, and both daemons' --check must accept the result. With the Protection bundle on it also writes protection.toml (connection caps, flood guard, EFnet DNSBL, spam protection, proxy scanner). It can make a self-signed certificate too. The same wizard is on the website (docs/wizard.html), running in the browser

Config templates rewritten to be easier to read: grouped by category with short headers, shorter comments, and the stale ones fixed (version, cloak format, ChanServ paths, REHASH). Newly documented: [server] sid, [[operators]] privileges and modes, [[classes]] sendq_max, [links] max_line_length. Every setting and default is unchanged
services.template.toml: removed a duplicated [link] header that made a straight copy of the template invalid TOML
ChanServ: an ACCESS entry by account (=account) now gives its mode when the user logs in to NickServ after joining the channel. Before, the mode only came on join, so identifying late meant a /cycle

Oper modes are configurable, like UnrealIRCd's modes-on-oper and Solanum's oper_umodes: [security] oper_modes (default "+osw") sets what every /OPER gets, and a login's own modes = "..." in [[operators]] replaces it (e.g. "+oswW" for a netadmin who wants WHOIS notices). o is always given; allowed on top are iwdTsBgZpIRD and the oper-only H, q and W. An unknown letter fails the config load. The MODE line after /OPER now lists only the modes that were actually added

Users who reach us over TLS through a web gateway or reverse proxy now get +z too, so they can join +z (TLS-only) channels: a WEBIRC with the IRCv3 "secure" option, and a WebSocket from a trusted_proxies address whose X-Forwarded-Proto is https at every hop. Direct TLS and wss connections already had it

REHASH now reports what it did. The oper gets 382 with the config path, then one "*** Rehash:" NOTICE per item: the config and Protection bundle files, which sections changed (or "no setting changed"), the MOTD/oper MOTD/rules files with their line counts, the spam-filter file with its rule count, any listener rebinds, and the TLS certificate reload. Other opers get a "<nick> is rehashing server config file" snotice

The MOTD, oper MOTD, rules and spam filters are yours, not git's: the repo now ships config/ircd.template.motd, oper.template.motd, ircd.template.rules and spamfilters.template.conf, and the live ircd.motd/oper.motd/ircd.rules/spamfilters.conf are untracked (.gitignore). The ircd creates a missing one from its template at start and on REHASH and never touches an existing one. Upgrading keeps your edited files as they are; a file you never edited is recreated from the new template. make install no longer overwrites an installed spamfilters.conf (it lost SPAMFILTER ADD rules on every reinstall)

MODE #chan from outside a keyed channel lost every argument after the hidden key: "+ntkl *" came back without the limit. Only the key is replaced with "*" now ("+ntkl * 5"). The 221 sent at connect also had a buffer too small for every user mode at once

Bans typed as a bare host or user@host now work. "+b 1.2.3.4", "+b *.example.com" and "+b baduser@host" used to be stored as-is and matched only against the nick, so they banned nobody. Masks are now stored in canonical form, as UnrealIRCd does it ("*!*@1.2.3.4", "*!baduser@host", "bob!*@*"), and -b finds them again
UnrealIRCd 6 named extbans are accepted: ~account:, ~quiet: or ~q:, ~realname:, ~channel: or ~c: are stored as our ~a:, ~m:, ~r: and ~j:
A MODE change that changes nothing (+n on a +n channel, -k with no key, +i when already invisible) is no longer broadcast, so client scripts that re-send modes stop flooding the channel

User modes now use UnrealIRCd's letters: +d is deaf (channel messages are not delivered to you, private ones still are) and +T drops CTCP sent to you, which +d used to do. If your [security] default_user_modes has a d, change it to T
New channel mode +K disables /KNOCK (480). New extban ~n:<mask> (UnrealIRCd's ~nickchange:) stops matching users from changing nick in the channel; voice and up are exempt
[security] default_user_modes accepted B and g but never applied them; it now does

The TLS user mode is now +z, as in UnrealIRCd, and +Z means private messages only to and from TLS users (531 otherwise; opers and services still get through). Linked servers still exchange it under the old letters, so a mixed-version network keeps working

+f takes UnrealIRCd's form too: [<n><type>[#<action>[<mins>]],...]:<secs>, with types c (CTCP), j (joins), k (knocks), m (messages), n (nick changes) and t (lines per user, kick or #b kick-ban). When a limit is passed the server sets the action mode (+C, +i, +K, +m, +N, or the alternative given) and removes it again after <mins> if a number is given. The plain <lines>:<secs> form still works
Timed bans: ~t:<minutes>:<mask> (or ~time:) on +b, +e or +I is removed by the server once the time is up, and works around any other mask, e.g. ~t:30:~m:*!*@host for a 30-minute quiet
New extban ~S:<fingerprint> (or ~certfp:) matches the SHA-256 fingerprint of a user's TLS client certificate
Ban, exception and invite-exception lists (367/348/346) now show who set each entry and when, as other ircds do

User mode +x: on by default under host_masking. -x shows your real host and +x cloaks it again (396 tells you the new host; CHGHOST goes to channel-mates). +x also works with host_masking off. Bans still match the real host and IP
User mode +W (opers only): a server notice whenever someone does a /WHOIS on you, from any server on the network
Forward bans: ~f:#chan:<mask> (or ~forward:) sends a matching user's JOIN to #chan instead of refusing it with 474
+f takes the r type too: the same line repeated <n> times by one user kicks them (#b kick-bans, #d just drops the line)

ChanServ takeover protection, as on Anope. ChanServ remembers each registered channel's TS. A channel recreated since it last saw it (on another server, during a netsplit, or while services were down) is reset: default modes, no +k/+i/+l/redirect, empty ban/exception/invite lists, then +r, MLOCK and a locked topic back. Anyone holding ops who isn't the founder, identified or on the access list at a level covering the rank loses them (SECUREOPS no longer needed for this). A channel with the TS it already knows, such as one a relinking server brings back, is left alone. On relink, ChanServ sweeps every registered channel, giving ACCESS modes and kicking AKICK/RESTRICTED members who joined meanwhile. ACCESS and AKICK work on JOIN in every registered channel, not only GUARDed ones. ChanServ can't be kicked or deopped (484). SECUREOPS checks each +o against the access level (a v entry no longer covers @). SJOIN with a TS of 0 or less no longer wins every channel. Mode changes that change nothing are no longer echoed

Fix (linked servers): a user joining a channel with members on another server also got that server's own topic and NAMES replies (331/332/353/366), once per remote server, and again when a server relinked. Only the user's own server answers a JOIN now

Fix: draft/multiline messages lost their line breaks and everything past 419 bytes in CHATHISTORY (they were stored as one flattened line, although up to 4096 bytes are accepted). History keeps the whole batch: clients with draft/multiline get it back as a multiline batch inside the chathistory batch, others as one message per line, as live
Fix: spam filters only checked the first 419 bytes of a multiline batch; the whole text is checked now

Fix: the user part was shown two ways. JOIN/PRIVMSG prefixes said ~user (ident not confirmed) while 001, WHOIS (311), WHO (352/354 u), NAMES with userhost-in-names (353), WHOWAS (314), USERHOST/USERIP (302), WATCH (604/600) and CHGHOST said user, so a ban copied from WHOIS (*!user@host) didn't match. All of them show the ~ now. ChanServ's NOTICEs no longer carry a ~ its MODE lines don't have. A CHGIDENT on a user on another server now reaches every server as a confirmed ident
labeled-response: REGISTER (draft/account-registration) answered ACK at once and sent REGISTER SUCCESS/FAIL unlabeled when services replied; the reply now carries the label and no ACK is sent
CHATHISTORY and MARKREAD without their capability (or with history off) answer FAIL ... INVALID instead of nothing
LIST: 321 is "321 nick Channel :Users  Name" (it was one trailing parameter)
[channels] default_modes defaults to "nt" when the key is missing, as the template says (it was empty, so channels took external messages)

draft/multiline across linked servers: a batch sent on one server reached users on the others as one flattened line cut at 419 bytes, and was stored that way in their CHATHISTORY. Its lines now travel with it (a new MLINE link line just before the message), so users on every server get the same multiline batch, or one message per line without the cap, and every server's history keeps it whole. Servers older than 1.3.2 ignore MLINE and still deliver the flattened message, so mixed networks keep working (a pre-1.3.2 server in the middle of a path flattens what passes through it)

tools/upgrade.py: when upstream rewrote its history (same code, new commit hashes) it said "diverged" and could not upgrade; it now says "same code as <commit> (upstream history was rewritten)" and moves the checkout onto upstream's history, keeping local edits. It also tells you when what runs isn't the checkout yet (bin/sekurircd older than the source, or a daemon started before the last build) and offers to rebuild and restart it. The menu's default is never an option older than your checkout (it was always [1], the latest release, even when that was a downgrade)

IRCv3: draft/event-playback. CHATHISTORY replays joins, parts, quits, kicks, mode and topic changes, nick changes and TAGMSG reactions (+draft/react, +draft/reply; never +typing) to clients that ask for it; other clients still get only messages, and their limits and references count only messages. [messages] history_events = false keeps messages only
IRCv3: draft/extended-isupport. The ISUPPORT command sends the 005 list on demand, also before registration, and with batch every 005 list comes in a draft/isupport batch
IRCv3: netsplit and netjoin batches. The quits of a split and the joins of a relink each come in one batch, so clients can fold them

IRCv3 UTF8ONLY: lines that aren't valid UTF-8 are refused with FAIL <command> INVALID_UTF8 and never relayed. On by default; [messages] utf8_only = false turns it off for networks with legacy-charset users
IRCv3: draft/ICON ([server] icon) and CLIENTTAGDENY ([messages] client_tag_deny) in 005; a +draft/channel-context tag is only relayed when it names a channel the sender is on
SASL re-authentication: a logged-in client may run SASL again to switch accounts (it got 907 before); a failed attempt keeps the current login

Event loop: kqueue (macOS/BSD) or epoll (Linux) instead of poll(), with a poll() fallback elsewhere. Each connection's interest is registered once and changed only when it changes, so a wakeup costs the number of busy connections instead of the number of connections; idle clients no longer slow everyone else down

REDACT (draft/message-redaction): take back a message still in history. Your own, or anyone's in a channel you operate (IRC operators too). It is removed from CHATHISTORY on every server, and clients with the cap hide it
PRIVMSG and NOTICE take up to 4 comma-separated targets (TARGMAX=PRIVMSG:4,NOTICE:4); each target counts against the flood limit and the spam limits like a separate message
Read markers take only the memory their key needs (they reserved 200 bytes each)

Fix: renaming a channel onto the name of a registered but empty channel walked past ChanServ, so the renamer kept op and the channel got no +r, MLOCK or SECUREOPS. A rename is now checked by services like a channel created by JOIN
Fix: spam filters skipped messages to ~#chan and &#chan (owners/admins only), treating them as private messages
Read markers (draft/read-marker) follow a channel RENAME; CHGIDENT re-checks SHUNs against the new ident
WHOIS: the 311 reply now includes the standard "*" field before the realname; strict clients (iSekur) failed to parse it without it

Spam filters: new hide and shun actions. hide drops a matching message silently: the sender gets no notice, and echo-message clients see it as sent. shun does the same and also SHUNs the sender's IP network-wide for the rule's duration. Opers are still notified
Linked servers: numeric replies now reach users on other servers. KNOCK reaches chanops on every server (it used to reach only those on the knocker's server)
WHOIS <nick> <nick> is answered by the user's own server, so idle time shows across links; MOTD, ADMIN, INFO, VERSION and TIME take a server name to ask that server
SHUN/UNSHUN are network-wide like GLINE (also sent to servers that link later); a SHUN set on one server used to do nothing to users on the others

KILL of a user on another server: the victim now gets the KILL line, and the quit reason names the oper (Killed (oper (reason))) the way a local KILL does; that server's opers get the 'Received KILL' notice
UNGLINE coming over a link removed the first line of any type with that mask, possibly a local K- or Z-line instead of the G-line. It now removes only the G-line
SQUERY to a service linked to another server reaches it (it used to be dropped silently)
Netsplits: a topic changed on one side during a split now survives the relink (the newer topic wins; it used to revert to the older one)
A leaf that dropped a dead link (ping timeout) waits until it is torn down before redialing, instead of refusing its own first reconnect and making the hub see an extra link up/down

IPv6 (opt-in): [server] ipv6 = true gives every listener (clients, TLS, WebSocket, server links) an IPv6 socket next to its IPv4 one. Off by default, so an upgrade changes nothing; separate IPv6-only sockets keep IPv4 clients and existing bans exactly as they were. IPv6 clients show as e.g. 2001:db8::5 (::1 as 0::1, since an IRC parameter can't start with ':'); reverse DNS, ident, DNSBL and link dialing work over IPv6; the proxy scanner stays IPv4-only

CIDR masks: K/G/Z-lines and E-lines, allowed_ips, oper hosts, WEBIRC/class/proxy hosts and protection exemptions take CIDR as well as globs (2001:db8::/32, 203.0.113.0/24). Per-IP limits, connect-flood auto-bans and host cloaks count an IPv6 client by its /64 (ipv6_limit_prefix), so rotating addresses inside it gets around none of them
Fix: every WEBIRC or X-Forwarded-For connection leaked one slot of the gateway's per-IP count, so a busy web chat gateway was eventually refused with "Too many connections from your host"

Link wizard: tools/linkmgmt.py add, edit and del now write this server's side of a link themselves: the [[links.peers]] block and any [links] changes, after showing the diff and asking. A private backup is kept, the ircd's own --check validates the result and a refused change is restored; then it rehashes the running ircd or says a restart is needed. The other server's side is still printed to paste there, and can be saved to a private file to copy over. --dry-run keeps the print-only behaviour
Testing: 139 end-to-end integration tests (IPv6 clients, CIDR bans, per-/64 limits, IPv6 links, rehash on/off, the gateway count fix)

Server links: pin each other's TLS certificate with fingerprint = "sha256:..." in [[links.peers]]. Self-signed certificates work without tls_insecure_skip_verify, a server that doesn't show the pinned certificate is refused before any password is sent or checked, and with a fingerprint the password is optional, so neither side has to keep a plain-text secret. The dialing server now presents its own [tls] certificate, and the accepting one asks for it
Server links: turning on [links] tls no longer cuts off the services daemon, which doesn't speak TLS: plain links are still accepted from 127.0.0.1, and only TLS from anywhere else

Passwords: tools/confcheck.py --fix --write turns plain-text passwords into scrypt password_hash lines (operators, die/restart, link peers the server only accepts from); the same passwords keep working. The ircd logs a reminder at start and on /REHASH while any are left

File permissions: confcheck warns about configs, the TLS key, account and ChanServ stores and --fix backups that other local users can read or change, with the exact chmod/chown for each case; --fix backups are now private (0600)
Tools: tools/linkmgmt.py fingerprint prints this server's certificate fingerprint, test HOST PORT --tls shows the other server's, and the add/edit wizard offers pinning
Testing: 132 end-to-end integration tests (pinned TLS links, wrong pins on either side, services over loopback)

Services: NickServ now runs in the services daemon next to ChanServ (bin/services, services 1.4.0) instead of inside every ircd. One account database for the whole network: every server relays SASL (PLAIN, SCRAM-SHA-256, EXTERNAL), REGISTER and PASS logins to it, so accounts can no longer diverge in a netsplit. Nick enforcement, GHOST and REGAIN work across servers; services admins are accounts listed in [nickserv] admins. While services are down, SASL is not offered and existing logins stay logged in

Upgrade: nothing to convert -- NickServ uses the existing config/accounts.json in place (the pre-upgrade file is kept as accounts.json.bak1); the old [accounts] section is ignored with a warning. Account and ChanServ stores keep rotating backups and never start empty over a corrupt file (they load the newest good backup or refuse to start)

Tools: ./sekurircd start|stop|restart|status manages the ircd and services (and retires an old standalone ChanServ); systemd services.service replaces chanserv.service and follows sekurircd.service; upgrade.py, make install, confcheck and the config backup handle the switch

Server linking: a server joining a large network no longer loses part of the burst (the link send queue was a fixed 32 KB); TLS links no longer stall the burst until the next PING; ChanServ's ops and UNBAN reach every server; SAJOIN/SAPART/SANICK/CHGHOST/CHGIDENT work on users of other servers; servers exchange their link protocol and version at handshake (compatible versions are announced to opers, incompatible ones refused)
Testing: 127 end-to-end integration tests (multi-server bursts, TLS links, services across servers, upgrade of old data)

NickServ: RESETPASS (emailed one-time code to the verified address, then a new password), REGAIN (take your nick back in one step), oper SUSPEND/UNSUSPEND, FDROP and SASET PASSWORD behind a new "accounts" oper privilege (suspensions replicate across linked servers and log the account out everywhere); /WHOIS NickServ answers as a network service; /NS, /NICKSERV, /CS and /CHANSERV shorthands. email_command now gets "verify" or "reset" as a fifth argument
Lower memory use: per-client lists allocated on demand, compact chat history, heap-allocated tables
Channel flood (+f) no longer counts TAGMSG, so typing indicators can't get anyone kicked

Web chat v2 (shared with www.sekurnet.org/chat/): home-screen app, tabs with close buttons, nick menu and colors, read markers, event icons, commands, /list dialog, typing indicators, desktop notifications, away/account markers, paste guard, text size and a hideable user list; new web chat docs page

Tools: tools/confcheck.py config validator (and sekurircd/chanserv --check; upgrade.py won't restart on a bad config), warns on a [server] name without a dot; upgrade.py can install systemd user units for clone installs
#server-debug: cleaner relay format, less connection noise
Testing: 115 end-to-end integration tests (5 new NickServ tests)
Fix: registered channels now get +r, MLOCK and GUARD back when they are recreated after dying or after a restart (services only restored them for channels that already existed when they linked)

Security: with SECUREOPS on, ChanServ strips ops/voice from anyone with no claim to them when a registered channel is recreated, and when services reconnect (channels recreated while services were down no longer keep their creator as op); new registrations have SECUREOPS on by default
Testing: 101 end-to-end integration tests

Security: fixed a use-after-free when a netsplit removed a chain of three or more servers, and IP spoofing through a WebSocket reverse proxy (X-Forwarded-For is now read right-to-left, skipping trusted proxies, instead of trusting the client-supplied leftmost entry)

Client compatibility: usernames like john.doe (the OS login irssi, WeeChat and HexChat send) are cleaned up instead of disconnecting the client; a full-length CAP REQ (gamja, Kiwi, Halloy) is no longer refused; MONITOR lists are split across lines instead of truncated; labeled responses no longer double-tag lines inside CHATHISTORY/multiline batches; STATUSMSG (@#chan) is echoed to echo-message clients; NAMES lines always fit in 512 bytes
New: WHO <mask> (nick, user, host, server, realname; 'o' for opers only), PASS account:password login for clients without SASL, and JOIN 0
Privacy: +i users no longer appear in WHO masks or in WHO #channel for people outside the channel

Fixes: RENAME keeps the channel's chat history; cap-notify sends correct SASL values (EXTERNAL when available, bare names to pre-302 clients); read markers and STATS m counters are bounded correctly; web chat nick fallback can no longer stall registration
Testing: 98 end-to-end integration tests (10 new client-compatibility tests)

Multi-server networking: SekurIRCd servers now link into a tree and share users, channels, modes, topics, bans, messages, away/account/host state and G-lines, with TS-based channel merging, nick-collision resolution, netsplit QUITs, /MAP, /LINKS, /SQUIT (also remote), /CONNECT, KILL/WALLOPS/GLOBOPS across servers and ChanServ serving users on any server. links.mode "both" with several [[links.peers]] and links.autoconnect
Accounts are replicated between linked servers (register, password, email, grouped nicks, drop; sent in the burst, last writer wins)

IRCv3: CAP 302/cap-notify, msgid, TAGMSG, batch, labeled-response, chathistory (server-level store with optional persistence and DM history), draft/multiline, draft/read-marker, draft/channel-rename, draft/no-implicit-names, draft/pre-away, extended-monitor, SASL SCRAM-SHA-256

Channel modes +f, +j, +L, +D, +u, +G, +q/+a ranks (~ and &); extbans ~r, ~z, ~j; caller-ID (+g/ACCEPT); connection classes; WEBIRC; PROXY protocol v1/v2; WebSocket (ws/wss) listener; oper privilege classes, SHUN, ELINE, GLOBOPS, SANICK, CHGIDENT, TESTLINE, LOCOPS, USERIP

NickServ: SET PASSWORD, DROP, LOGOUT, INFO, SET EMAIL/VERIFY, GROUP/UNGROUP, GHOST and nick enforcement. ChanServ: account-based founder, SECUREOPS, RESTRICTED, PRIVATE, LIST, extended MLOCK, owner/admin ranks

Hardening from the 2026-10 audit (stale worker results, link allowed_ips, +P abuse, NOTICE auto-replies, ISUPPORT/protocol fixes, link/worker robustness) and rehash now rebinds listeners and reloads the TLS certificate
Testing: 88-test end-to-end integration suite (make itest, including 3-server networks), clean under ASan/UBSan, plus a parser fuzz harness (make fuzz)

Security audit: fixed a TLS handshake busy-loop DoS, umode +q (unkickable) being settable by any user instead of opers only, a proxy-scanner flood/cap-limit bypass, and hostname K/G-lines and channel bans that silently never matched (rDNS result and bans now check the real host/IP, not just a possibly-cloaked displayed one)
Security: new per-IP throttle on SASL/NickServ IDENTIFY, a timing-safe decoy for unknown accounts, and a fix for a second login attempt applying its result to the wrong pending account
Security: /REGISTER's instant self-service account creation no longer grants full spam-check exemption immediately; accounts.json/klines.json are now written 0600 with fsync-before-rename
Bugfix: use-after-free on self-KICK/SAPART, case-only nick changes never being announced, and SAJOIN/auto_join handing out ops on a channel it didn't actually create

ChanServ: SUCCESSOR CLAIM now checks a claimant's real identity over the link instead of the (possibly cloaked) PRIVMSG sender host, so a hostmask or "=account" successor actually works; identified-founder state now expires and is cleared on DROP/reconnect instead of occasionally sticking forever and permanently blocking a legitimate CLAIM; AKICK now also sets a ban; several crash/data-loss fixes in the JSON store
New channel modes +R (registered-only join), +O (oper-only join), +M (registered/voice+ only speak), +c (reject colour/formatting outright)
New quiet extban m:/~m: (blocks speaking, not joining); ~a: alias for the existing a:account extban; /LIST now matches a #-prefixed pattern and a leading ! negates
New ChanServ commands: OP/DEOP/VOICE/DEVOICE/HALFOP/DEHALFOP, INVITE, UNBAN, KICK, TOPIC
New IRCv3 STS support ([tls] sts_duration)

Performance: O(1) worker-result lookup (was O(n) per result, O(n^2) across a connect burst) and a send buffer that shrinks back down after a large burst instead of staying at its peak size for the connection's life

New Protection bundle: an optional, one-file abuse-protection layer (config/protection.toml, template in config/protection.template.toml) that groups DNSBL blacklists, the new proxy scanner, connection limits, the connect-flood throttle, the per-client flood guard and spam protection. Leave the file out and nothing changes

Active open-proxy scanner ([scanner], off by default): on connect the server tries HTTP CONNECT, HTTP POST, SOCKS4 and SOCKS5 back through the client's own address to its own public address; a working relay bans the address and drops everyone connected from it. Runs in the background on non-blocking sockets in the main loop, with a per-probe timeout, a concurrency cap and an optional negative cache

DNSBL blacklists moved into the bundle ([blacklist]) and gained per-zone reply rules: exact or bitmask reply codes, ban_unknown, and a per-zone ban reason with %i/%t/%r placeholders. The old [dnsbl] section keeps working and logs a deprecation warning

Connection caps, the connect-flood throttle, the flood guard and [spam] can now live in the bundle file ([connection], [flood], [spam]); where the bundle sets a key it overrides sekurircd.toml, and the old keys still work
[exempt] lists IP globs that are never DNSBL-checked or scanned; connections a scan relays back to the server are exempt from the connect-flood throttle and per-IP cap
New oper command /PROTECT shows the bundle's state and counters; /PROTECT SCAN <ip> scans an address on demand. /VERSION shows a P flag for the scanner
Bundle activity is logged with the protection/dnsbl tags and relayed into your debug channel: bans, a startup/REHASH summary and the periodic stats line now include proxy-scanner counters
A DNSBL hit now also disconnects every other connection from that address; the server sends the standard NOTICE AUTH "*** Looking up your hostname" line on connect
Docs: new Protection bundle page and config template
Security: fixed a remotely-triggerable stack buffer overflow in channel MODE handling, reachable by any channel operator
Security: ident/rDNS/DNSBL lookups are now bounded by their configured timeouts (dnsbl.timeout and rdns_timeout were previously ignored) and can no longer stall the worker pool
Security: bans, /SILENCE and ChanServ ACCESS/AKICK now match identd-confirmed users correctly; a mask written the way WHOIS displays a user finally bites
KLINE/GLINE now match host and user@host masks, not just IPs; ZLINE stays IP-only for connect-time bans
Security: constant-time password comparison for OPER/DIE/RESTART and server links; hardened build flags (stack protector, FORTIFY_SOURCE, RELRO/BIND_NOW on Linux)
INVITE can no longer be used to send arbitrary text around /SILENCE, +D and +R
Fixed an out-of-descriptors condition that pegged a CPU core, and a lost auth result that permanently wedged a connection's ability to log in
/REGISTER is rate-limited and the account store is capped ([accounts] max_accounts)
Config validation no longer overflows on a bad host_masking_token_bytes; max_params, max_nick_length and max_message_length are range-checked
Performance: O(1) per-IP connection counting, deduplicated and batched K-line writes, debounced ChanServ store writes
A leaf server reconnect no longer freezes the event loop for the OS connect timeout
SASL EXTERNAL: log in with a TLS client certificate, bound with /CERT ADD
Z-lines (ZLINE/UNZLINE), /WATCH, and STATS k/g/z/l
Per-IP connect-flood throttle that auto-bans scanners
Server-notice (+s) alerts for OPER, failed OPER, KILL, links, and SA*/SETHOST overrides
Optional oper host masking on /OPER, human-friendly ban expiry and uptime
Rootless systemd user units, make install/uninstall, and a start/stop/status wrapper script
Hardened server-link listener; random RPL_YOURID
New /RULES command backed by config/ircd.rules, and an operator MOTD (config/oper.motd) sent on /OPER and via /OPERMOTD; both reload on /REHASH
New [messages] keys: oper_motd and rules; templates for both files are included

New spam protection module ([spam], off by default): regex content filters for PRIVMSG/NOTICE (users and channels) plus AWAY, QUIT, PART and TOPIC text; a new-connection restriction on PMs; and recipient/repeat limits that catch bots messaging many targets
Filters live in config/spamfilters.conf (an example file is included) with actions block, warn, kill and zline; filters_enabled turns the file off without touching the rest
New /SPAMFILTER LIST|ADD|DEL oper command edits the filters file live; regexes are validated (no backreferences, no empty matches); rules reload on /REHASH
Opers with +s get a notice for every spam action, and services, opers and identified accounts are exempt by default

/VERSION is now ircu/solanum-style: SekurIRCd-<version>(<date>-<commit>) plus feature flags and the full 005 ISUPPORT list; WHOX and MAXCHANNELS are now advertised, and 004 carries the same build string

Accounts: IRCv3 draft/account-registration (REGISTER <account|*> <email|*> <password>) and a built-in NickServ (REGISTER / IDENTIFY) alongside /REGISTER and SASL; registering while already logged in is now refused
User mode +B marks a client as a bot (IRCv3 bot mode): 335 in WHOIS, B in WHO flags, @bot message tag, BOT=B in 005
Periodic stats server notice for opers
ChanServ bug fixes
README rewritten as a standalone project doc
Fixed crashes, security holes and performance stalls; wired up previously dead config options
New channel and user modes: +P +C +T +S +V +Q +N
Fixed the Linux build (glibc POSIX gating) and added a TLS connect notice
Expanded ChanServ HELP; fixed OPER re-auth and TOPICLOCK sync; WHOX support
Initial release of the C port
